entry.focal: The near white post on the right, then the hero cable-station box at centre, flanked by posts lights0:0/lights1:0. The station is a dark, unlit brown box; the flanking posts read as a gate, which helps.
entry.next_visible: The pool's water and lantern line on the left, and a second dark box with lit windows (the cable station/neighbour) across the water.

reveal.focal: The close white post in the lower-left foreground (lights1:1 at 80.2, 62.9) dominates, and two noisy white mist domes sit in the water. The hero is a dark box at the right edge with a post standing in front of its door.
reveal.next_visible: The pool, island_w (grey cube) and the north-side lanterns. The pool is a good destination cue, but nothing leads the eye to it.

concept.focal: island_w (grey cube on a slab) in the middle of the pool. The lower 40% of the frame is black empty foreground. The intended match (lantern-lined boardwalk on black rock, islands below left, spring lanterns far right) does not appear: the camera points straight across the pool, so the boardwalk is out of frame.

strip.focal: A continuous, evenly spaced row of identical white posts, often doubled where both rows coincide. There is no landmark until the moon pavilion box appears in frames 4-7 (good), and a white slab cuts the right edge in frame 7.
strip.next_visible: Yes: the moon pavilion with lit windows from frame 4 on, and the pool to the right. The spring and the cliff stair head never register as places.

fixes.detail: offset 0.8 -> 1.5 on both rows: the posts stand inside the 3.4 m deck, and where the rows pair up (lights0:0/1:0, 0:5/1:3, 0:9/1:4, 0:10/1:5) the clear width drops to about 1.6 m. Replace even spacing [6,9] with node clusters: 2-3 posts at each event (cable station door, rill bridge, spring steps p_s_rim_spring, pool_n portal, cliff stair head, moon steps) and [12,16] dark gaps between. Drop lights[1] (the pool side) except at the two pool portals.

Both rules produced 0 placements, so 120 m of boardwalk carries only posts and invisible rails. Fix the rules and weight them to the outer (drop) side at corners and nodes: pines at the SW corner (about 75, 64), the NW corner (about 81, 103) and beside the cliff stair head; rock clusters at the rill bridge abutments.
It sits on the pool (south) side of the walk, but the Cliff Stair leaves to the north (portal at 140, 107). Move it to the stair mouth's west flank (about 138.2, 107.9), facing the walker.

Same problem: move it to the stair mouth's east flank (about 142.0, 107.8) so sign and toro bracket the stair. It is the only wayfinding cue for a whole descent route and currently reads as one more post on the wrong side.

Turn the concept camera from looking south across the pool to looking west along the north arm (target about 92, 104, 120.5), so the lantern-lined boardwalk recedes with the pool and islands below on the left, as in plan 30.

top_change: Break the 120 m runway of evenly spaced posts into lit nodes at the cable station, rill bridge, spring steps, cliff stair and moon steps, with darker stretches and edge pines/rocks between, so the walk has destinations instead of a uniform lantern line.
plausibility: Railings are not visible in any frame on a crater-lip walk with a drop on the outer side. The pieces are 1.5 m long at about 4.5-5 m pitch, which leaves 3 m gaps, and z = floor + 1.0 may mean they float.

The west leg of s_rim (x 74-78) runs parallel to s_pool's west deck spine (x 82.5), 5-8 m apart, so two lantern-lined walks shadow each other along the pool. In the strips they read as one wide undefined platform. Either merge them or separate them with the 1.5 m retaining wall/planting.
The outer edge shows no drop: the terrain beyond the rail is flat at walk level, so 'always a drop or rock wall on the other side' does not read.
